answer.label: Bill Murray credit unsupported
answer.sourceLine: PolitiFact’s 2020 investigation rejected the Murray attribution and identified an earlier 2015 tweet without a celebrity credit. It also distinguished a genuine 2018 Murray interview about social media from these different words. The exact sentence’s creator remains unconfirmed; agreement with its sentiment cannot establish authorship.

context.heading: The setting behind the words
lead: Murray did make separate comments criticizing the urge to document an experience instead of living it. The checked 2018 interview gives those different words, not the viral sentence about comparison and depression. Similar subject matter is why the false credit can sound plausible while remaining unsupported. PolitiFact attribution investigation ↗
